scientific_findings: The main thesis remains executable historical-data acceptance contracts. The numeric and authorization cases express distinct acceptance boundaries rather than claimed new defects or repair algorithms.

AI SDK attribution points to the genuine public upstream PR. The text explicitly says known serialization ambiguity, not a newly discovered HMAC collision; it does not claim end-to-end authorization or an extra Gemma task.

The 54 related scenarios, 27 legacy and 27 fresh cases, 54 initial plus 54 fresh-process verifications per implementation, and 37 separately contract-eligible reissues are correctly distinguished. Reissue eligibility explicitly does not depend on the control's actual initial acceptance.

Table 2 matches all five score files by expected-accept, expected-reject and total groups. The lower three implementations are clearly labeled researcher-written controls. The text correctly states that restart adds no scenario rejections.
The old 32-attempt, two-deployment baseline remains distinct from the new 64-attempt controlled campaign. Table 1 retains A=1/16, B=3/16; no pooled improvement is claimed.

The new primary result is exact-text 10/32 versus version-checked spans 4/32. All eight lineage points agree with analysis. Whole-package scope, nested repetitions, selected public tasks and the lack of a general editor ranking are stated.
The 49 syntax/indentation rejections across 15 span attempts match the completed independent mechanics audit. The text explicitly declines causal attribution of the acceptance gap to those errors.

Both reviewed engineering recoveries, all 64 complete-acceptance decisions remaining stable, four partial dtype observation drifts, and both reported and conservative API costs are disclosed accurately.
The resource card separates the 252 original observations, 32 baseline attempts, 64 new attempts and 54 signature scenarios. The text does not treat those repetitions as independent defects.
SWE-Edit's official arXiv title, first author and scope support reference 17 and the modest related-work claim. This check is not a new exhaustive re-audit of all previously reviewed references.
